br.br:
1. An apparatus for capturing a video of a human patient suitable for monitoring a cardiac, respiratory or cardiorespiratory condition, the apparatus comprising:an electronic imager, the imager positionable with respect to a neck of the patient to be able to capture electronic video of the neck of the patient;
a locator object external to the body of the patient, the locator object structured to be repeatedly stably positionable on the body of the patient with respect to an anatomic location on a torso of the patient, the locator object being connected to the imager; and a reference element, the reference element being positionable with respect to the neck of the patient by positioning of the locator object.
2. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the locator object is connected to the imager such that, when the locator object is positioned on the body of the patient with respect to the anatomic location on the torso of the patient, both the neck of the patient and at least part of the reference element are simultaneously able to be captured in the video by the imager without movement of the imager.
3. The apparatus of claim 2, wherein the locator object is connected to the imager such that, when the locator object is positioned on the body of the patient with respect to the anatomic location on the torso of the patient, both the neck of the patient and an entirety of the reference element are simultaneously able to be captured in the video by the imager without movement of the imager.
4. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 3, wherein the reference element is the locator object.
5. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 3, wherein the reference element is structured electro-magnetic (EM) radiation projected onto the neck of the patient.
6. The apparatus of claim 5, wherein the structured EM radiation is projected from the locator object.
7. The apparatus of claim 6, wherein the structured EM radiation is projected from a projector fixedly mechanically linked to the locator object.
8. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 3, wherein the reference element is a physical structure directly attached to the locator object.
9. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 3, wherein the reference element is a physical structure fixedly mechanically linked to the locator object.
10. The apparatus of any one of claims 2 to 9, wherein the neck of the patient includes at least one of an internal jugular vein and an external jugular vein of the patient, and the locator object is connected to the imager such that the when the locator object is positioned on the body of the patient with respect to the anatomic location on the torso of the patient, both (i) an area of the skin of the neck overlying the at least one of the internal jugular vein and the external jugular vein of the patient, and(ii) the at least part of the reference element are simultaneously able to be captured in the video by the imager without movement of the imager.
11. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 10, wherein the anatomic location of the torso of the patient is at least one of the patient's sternum, sternal angle, manubrium, clavicular heads and suprasternal notch.
12. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 11, wherein the connection between the locator object and the imager is a mechanical connection.
13. The apparatus of claim 12, wherein the connection between the locator object and the imager is fixed.
14. The apparatus of claims 12 to 13, wherein the connection between the locator object and the imager includes a member fixedly attached to the locator object, the member being alignable with a landmark of the torso of the patient during positioning of the locator object with respect to the anatomic location on the torso of the patient.
15. The apparatus of claim 1 to 14, wherein the connection between the locator object and the imager includes an electronic connection.
16. The apparatus of claim 15, wherein the electronic connection is via a computer processor.
17. The apparatus of any one of claims 15 to 16, wherein the electronic connection includes a wireless connection.
18. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 17, wherein the locator object has a sensor for sensing at least one physiological parameter of the patient, the sensor being in electronic communication with the imager.
19. The apparatus of claim 18, wherein data from the sensor is synchronizable with data from the imager.
20. The apparatus of any one of claims 18 to 19, wherein the sensor is at least one of a contact sensor, an electrocardiogram (ECG) electrode, and a pulse oximeter.
21. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 20, wherein the locator object has a spherical portion dimensioned to contact the patient's suprasternal notch.
22. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 21, wherein the locator object has an interchangeable patient-contacting element.
23. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 22, wherein the locator object has at least one adjustable patient-contacting element.
24. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 23, wherein the locator object has markings that provide a scale of measurement.
25. The apparatus of claim 24, wherein the locator object has markings that provide multiple scales of measurement.
26. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 25, further comprising a sensor providing information relevant to the determination of an angle of inclination of the locator object when the locator object is stably positioned on the body of the patient with respect to the anatomic location on the torso of the patient.
27. The apparatus of claim 26, wherein the sensor is at least one of an accelerometer and a gyroscope fixed in orientation with respect to the locator object.
28. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 27, wherein the apparatus is structured to rest on the torso of the patient when in use capturing the video.
29. The apparatus of claim 28, wherein the apparatus has a portion that is shaped to conform to a portion of the torso of the patient such that the portion of the apparatus rests on the portion of the torso of the patient when the apparatus is in use capturing the video.
30. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 29, further comprising an articulated arm having a first end movably connected to a base station and a second end movably connected to the imager.
31. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 30, further comprising at least two electrodes for contacting the skin of the patient in order to generate an electrocardiogram (ECG) signal.
32. The apparatus of claim 31, wherein a first one of the at least two electrodes is on the locator object and a second one of the at least two electrodes is on a handgrip spaced apart from the locator object.
33. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 32, further comprising, a computer processor in electronic communication with the imager;an information storage medium in electronic communication with the computer processor; and
a wireless transceiver in electronic communication with the computer processor.
34. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 33, further comprising a microphone.
35. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 34, further comprising a speaker.
36. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 35, further comprising a user-actuated sensor element operatively connected to the imager to control video capture by the imager.
37. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 36, further comprising, an electromagnetic radiation source providing electromagnetic radiation in at least the near infrared (NIR) spectrum; anda filter allowing for the selective passage of electromagnetic radiation in the NIR spectrum to the imager.
38. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 37, wherein the electronic imager is a first electronic imager; andfurther comprising a second electronic imager fixed in position with respect to the first electronic imager.
39. The apparatus of claim 38, wherein the first electronic imager is an NIR spectrum imager and the second electronic imager is a visible light spectrum imager.
40. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 39, wherein the reference element has predetermined dimensions that render a height of the column of blood in a jugular vein of the patient with respect to at least one of the patient's sternal angle and another grossly immobile anatomic feature of the patient's torso determinable by a computer processor from the captured electronic video.
41. The apparatus of claim 40, wherein another grossly immobile anatomic feature of the patient's torso is one of a patent's clavicular head, suprasternal notch, and sternum.
42. The apparatus of any one of claims 40 to 41, wherein the height of the column of blood in the jugular vein of the patient with respect to at least one of the patient's sternal angle and another grossly immobile anatomic feature of the patient's upper body is determinable by the computer processor from the captured electronic video without having reference to a different image of the neck of the patient and without requiring the imager having been fixed in a precise position with respect to the neck of the patient at the time that the electronic video was captured.
43. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 42, wherein the imager is not in direct contact with the patient.
44. The apparatus of any one of claims 1 to 43, wherein the imager is not held in a fixed position by a connection to the patient.
45. A method of capturing an electronic video of a human patient suitable for monitoring a cardiac, respiratory or cardiorespiratory condition, via an apparatus including, an electronic imager, the imager being positionable with respect to a neck of the patient to be able to capture the electronic video of the neck of the patient, a locator object external to the body of the patient, the locator object being structured to be repeatedly stably positionable on the body of the patient with respect to an anatomic location on a torso of the patient, the locator object being connected to the imager, and a reference element, the reference element being positionable with respect to the neck of the patient by positioning of the locator object, 73
the method comprising,
positioning the apparatus with respect to the patient such that the imager is positionable with respect to the neck of the patient to be able to capture the electronic video of the neck of the patient;
positioning the locator object in a stable position on the body of the patient with respect to the anatomic location on the torso of the patient, thereby causing at least one of the reference elements and the imager to be positioned with respect to the neck of the patient such that the neck of the patient and at least part of the reference element are simultaneously able to be captured in the electronic video by the imager without movement of the imager; and
causing the electronic video to be captured by the imager.
46. The method of claim 45, wherein positioning the locator object in a stable position on the body of the patient with respect to the anatomic location on the torso of the patient, causes both of the reference element and the imager to be positioned with respect to the neck of the patient such that the neck of the patient and at least part of the reference element are simultaneously able to be captured in the electronic video by the imager without movement of the imager.
47. An apparatus, comprising:a positioning element configured to fit within a suprasternal notch of a patient;
a reference element having a known size;
an imaging assembly coupled to and spaced from the positioning element, the imaging assembly configured to capture imaging data of at least a portion of a neck of a patient and a portion of the reference element; and a processor operatively coupled to the imaging assembly, the processor configured to determine a jugular venous pressure (JVP) or height information associated with the neck of the patient based on the imaging data and the known size of the reference element.
48. The apparatus of claim 47, wherein the positioning element includes the reference element.
49. The apparatus of any one of claims 47-48, wherein the positioning element including a spherical portion that is configured to fit within the suprasternal notch of the patient.
50. The apparatus of any one of claims 47-49, wherein the positioning element is a first positioning element, the apparatus further comprising a second positioning element configured to rest against a portion of a chest of a patient.
51. The apparatus of any one of claims 47-50, wherein the positioning element, the reference element, and the imaging assembly are disposed on a sensing device, and the processor is disposed within a base,the base including a surface including a set of structures configured to receive a portion of the sensing device and to stably support the sensing device on the surface of the base.
52. The apparatus of any one of claims 47-51, wherein the imaging assembly is coupled to the positioning element such that, when the positioning element is positioned within the suprasternal notch, the imaging assembly can be positioned to capture the imaging data of the at least the portion of the neck of the patient and the portion of the reference element.
53. The apparatus of any one of claims 47-52, wherein the imaging assembly includes a near infrared (NIR) light source configured to emit NIR light toward the neck of the patient and a NIR camera configured to capture NIR light reflected by the neck of the patient.
54. The apparatus of any one of claims 47-53, wherein the imaging assembly includes first and second cameras, each of the first and second cameras configured to capture light in different wavelength ranges.
55. The apparatus of claim 54, wherein the first camera is configured to capture optical light, and the second camera is configured to capture NIR light.
56. The apparatus of any one of claims 47-53, wherein the imaging assembly includes first and second cameras configured to capture light in the same wavelength ranges to provide stereovision.
57. The apparatus of any one of claims 47-56, wherein the processor is configured to determine the JVP or height information associated with the neck of the patient by:determining, based on the portion of the reference element captured in the image data, a conversion between pixels of the imaging data and a physical measure of distance.
58. The apparatus of any one of claims 47-56, wherein the processor is configured to determine the JVP or height information associated with the neck of the patient by:determining, based on the portion of the reference element captured in the image data, a conversion between pixels of the imaging data and a physical measure of distance;
determining, from the imaging data, a highest point of a pulsation of an internal jugular vein (IJV) of the patient; and
determining, based on at least the conversion between the pixels of the imaging data and the physical measure of distance, a vertical height between a sternal angle and the highest point of the pulsation of the IJV of the patient.
59. The apparatus of claim 58, further comprising at least one of an accelerometer or a gyroscope configured to measure an orientation of a neck of a patient relative to a horizontal plane,wherein the determination of the vertical height is further based on an angle of inclination of the neck of the patient as determined based on the measured orientation of the neck.
60. The apparatus of any one of claims 47-56, wherein the processor is configured to determine the JVP of the patient by:determining, based on a static image of the portion of the neck of the patient and a portion of the apparatus, an angle of a longitudinal axis of the neck relative to an angle of the apparatus;
determining, from the imaging data, a highest point of pulsation of an internal jugular vein (IJV) of the patient; and
determining, based on the angle of the longitudinal axis of the neck and highest point of pulsation of the IJV, a vertical height between a sternal angle and the highest point of the pulsation of the IJV of the patient.
61. The apparatus of any one of claims 47-60, further comprising an actuator configured to be actuated by the patient to cause the processor to activate the imaging assembly to capture the imaging data.
62. The apparatus of any one of claims 47-61, further comprising one or more sensors including at least one of an electrocardiogram sensor, a photoplethysmography sensor, an electrodermal activity sensor, or a temperature sensor.
63. The apparatus of claim 62, wherein the one or more sensors are disposed on a body coupled to the imaging assembly and the positioning element such that, when the patient grips the body for positioning of the positioning element relative to the suprasternal notch, a portion of a hand of the patient is in contact with the one or more sensors to facilitate measurement by the one or more sensors.
64. The apparatus of claim 62, wherein the one or more sensors are disposed on a body coupled to the imaging assembly and the positioning element such that, when the positioning element is positioned relative to the suprasternal notch, the one or more sensors are in contact with a skin of the patient to facilitate measurement by the one or more sensors.
